lines: Stopped the job, then refused to call it fixed when the job came back. Escalated to the pricing team, and remembered the lesson.

events.caption: checkout starts failing (4 timed out so far).

tech.title: Checkout degraded: 4 timeouts since injection, success 0%
12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 12083 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s)

Checkout success 75% over 10s (8/32 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,600/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

detail.rationale: The root blocker (pid 12083, batch_replayable_price_sync) has held its transaction for only 4.0s [DB-1]. Checkout is degraded (53% success over 15s [TEL-2], 75% over 10s [BIZ-3]) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation [BIZ-3]. Memory shows a prior verified pact where terminating a similar batch_replayable workload (inventory_reconcile) restored checkout [MEM-4], but that was a different job and the Continuity Guardian required evidence before accepting. We lack the workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, and tradeoff data needed to assess interrupt safety and cost. Requesting those probes first is lower risk than acting blindly.

tech.title: R1 after investigating: switches to terminate:batch_replayable_price_sync

detail.rationale: The root blocker pid 12083 (batch_replayable_price_sync) has held its transaction for 4.0s [DB-1]. Checkout is severely degraded at 23% success over 30s [BIZ-8] with $14,204/min revenue at risk. The tradeoff analysis shows waiting costs ~$141,088 (596s remaining runtime) and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-9]. The workload is replayable with 2-minute replay cost and policy may_interrupt [BIZ-5]. No protected settlements in flight [DB-7] and no active change calendar window [BIZ-6]. Memory shows terminating a similar batch_replayable workload (inventory_reconcile) restored checkout [MEM-4].

tech.title: R1 ACCEPT

detail.business_rationale: Checkout is at 23% success (BIZ-8) with $14,204/min revenue at risk. Waiting for the blocker's ~596s remaining runtime would cost ~$141,088 and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-9). The blocker is a replayable batch job (price_sync) with a 2-minute replay cost and may_interrupt policy (BIZ-5). No protected settlements are in flight (DB-7) and no active change-calendar window requires owner consultation (BIZ-6). Terminating the blocker releases locks immediately; checkout should recover within seconds and the job will replay automatically.
